name: Concourse Plaza
summary: Concourse Plaza is a vibrant 247,000-square-foot mixed-use destination in the Bronx, anchored by Food Bazaar supermarket and a new Regal cinema with 10 screens. Located steps from Yankee Stadium and the subway, it combines community-oriented retail, diverse dining, office space, and essential services in a recently modernized facility.
demographics: Concourse Plaza serves a diverse, predominantly Hispanic and Caribbean community in the South Bronx, with a trade area characterized by working-class and middle-income households. The center attracts a broad age range from young families to seniors, with many visitors relying on public transportation from the nearby 174-175th Street subway station. Primary shoppers include value-conscious consumers seeking everyday essentials, entertainment, and community services, with strong foot traffic from Yankee Stadium visitors and local office workers. The demographic mix reflects the cultural richness of the Concourse Village neighborhood, with shopping patterns emphasizing grocery, affordable dining, and family-oriented entertainment options.
description: Concourse Plaza stands as a vital mixed-use destination in the heart of the Bronx's Concourse Village neighborhood, strategically positioned at 200 E. 161st Street just steps from Yankee Stadium and the historic Grand Concourse. Originally constructed in 1990, this 247,000-square-foot center has undergone significant modernization in recent years, transforming its façade, interior layouts, and energy systems to create a contemporary shopping and office environment flooded with natural light and enhanced accessibility. The center is anchored by Food Bazaar, a 52,000-square-foot supermarket offering international and local brands, and the newly opened Regal Concourse cinema, which features 10 state-of-the-art screens with reclining seats across 58,000 square feet. Beyond retail, Concourse Plaza serves as a true community hub with over 1,200 parking spaces, office suites ranging from 4,100 to 22,000 square feet housing government agencies and healthcare providers, and diverse dining options including Burger King, Popeye's, Hook & Reel, and NYY Steak. The center's commitment to community engagement shines through regular events like health fairs and cultural celebrations, partnerships with local nonprofits supporting Hispanic- and Caribbean-owned businesses, and sustainability initiatives including energy-efficient systems and comprehensive recycling programs, all while maintaining exceptional transit connectivity via the B and D subway lines.
